inventory.label: the half-ramp shoot (first of the year)
inventory.notes: Year's first green, foraged from a warm-soil patch six steps south of the leaning birch by the brook. YY ate half on the spot, tucked the other half into his cheek to carry.

identity_notes: Late winter — YY is hungry but has eaten the year's first food and carries the second half.
Yesterday: foraged the year's first ramp shoot from a hidden warm patch south of the brook; ate half, tucked half in his cheek.
Today: heard the brook running brown after an upstream icejam broke; scampered to the eddy and pulled out a cluster of soaked beechnuts; ate one kernel, tucked another in his cheek.
Standing thread: the warm patch is still hidden and unread.
Late winter — YY ate the carry-half ramp shoot at the treehouse last night; the inventory is empty again.
Yesterday: dug up the year's first ramp shoot from the hidden warm patch and brought half home.

Today: the brook surged brown after an upstream icejam broke; YY went paws-out at the eddy and rescued a cluster of soaked beechnuts. One kernel was good and ate it on the spot. The half-cold from the dive is sitting in his chest tonight.
Standing thread: the warm patch is still hidden; the brook only carries once.

change_summary.notable_shift: First active forage from a moving brook. Gain came from commitment — a paws-out dive at the eddy, cold-spray paid up front. The shift confirms that this branch trades momentary exposure for moving food.
